decisions.quote: I was able to fully replicate the significance of this difference, but the finding is not as robust as the original, as reflected in the weaker evidence shown in the p values and F values. The figure I produced from the replication also looks qualitatively similar to the original, but the original did not provide error bars or discuss standard error of the mean or confidence intervals, so I’m not entirely sure how similar the figures are in terms of data variability. Commentary Interestingly, even though I was able to replicate the original study’s finding regarding affect, my exploratory analysis did not find that attitude was more negative toward Asian Americans when realistic threat was induced. My replication indicates that inducing realistic threat influences emotion, but not attitudes, towards Asian Americans.
decisions.location: OSF Primary Source: maddux2008.html, Discussion -> Summary of Replication Attempt & Commentary (texts/2736b815e9f115a4.txt, line 636); see also raw_data.csv line 234
decisions.reason: In maddux2008.html (replicating Maddux, Galinsky, Cuddy, & Polifroni, 2008, Study 3, DOI 10.1177/0146167207309195; paired_target_index 35), the original Study 3 demonstrated that realistic threat caused both negative attitude (7-point bipolar scale, the "main attitude measure") and negative affect (0-100 feeling thermometer) toward Asian Americans. The replication author replicated the significant difference on the affect thermometer (F(1, 76) = 4.779, p = .032, eta2 = .060), but also administered and tested the original Study 3 attitude scale (finding no significant difference, F(1, 76) = 1.564, p = .215, eta2 = .020) and explicitly contrasted this non-replication with the original Study 3 finding in the Discussion Commentary: "even though I was able to replicate the original study’s finding regarding affect, my exploratory analysis did not find that attitude was more negative toward Asian Americans when realistic threat was induced. My replication indicates that inducing realistic threat influences emotion, but not attitudes, towards Asian Americans." Under Codebook Rule 1 and Rule 2, confirming one focal effect ("I was able to fully replicate the significance of this difference") is one comparison rather than an overall verdict on the replication as a whole, and a tested original finding that the report itself explicitly contrasts with the original cannot be left out of the verdict even if labeled exploratory relative to the single focal class assignment test. Furthermore, the full primary report overrides the single-test 1/1 summary row in raw_data.csv. Thus both shipped and blind "successful" codings are wrong, and the corrected value is "mixed".

decisions.quote: We succesfully replicated the key finding of Tworek and Cimpian (2016). The predicted interaction between inherence bias and behavior typicality was significant in the fitted model (bb = 3.737, 95% CI = [2.512, 4.96], p<.001p<.001). The predicted interaction between behavior typicality and conservatism was also significant (b=b= 2.213, 95% CI = [1.186, 3.239], p<.001p<.001). In the original study, conservatism was also a significant predictor, but was not in this replication.

The predicted interaction between inherence bias and behavior typicality was significant in the fitted model (bb = 3.737, 95% CI = [2.512, 4.96], p<.001p<.001). The predicted interaction between behavior typicality and conservatism was also significant (b=b= 2.213, 95% CI = [1.186, 3.239], p<.001p<.001). In the original study, conservatism was also a significant predictor, but was not in this replication." Under Codebook Rule 1 and Rule 2, a sentence confirming "the key finding" speaks only to that focal comparison rather than the replication as a whole, and because the author explicitly contrasts a tested original finding from the same fitted model that did not replicate ("In the original study, conservatism was also a significant predictor, but was not in this replication"), the outcome across the explicitly contrasted original findings in the primary report is "mixed", overriding the single-effect 1/1 rating in raw_data.csv. Thus both shipped and blind "successful" codings are wrong, and the corrected value is "mixed".
